solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Popular German car briefly ran making no noticeable sound (9)

indicatorNotes.briefly: something said briefly is cut short, so BLED loses its last letter

blocks.note: Audi is a German car maker
colours that ran in the wash have bled

annotation.surface: A trendy German car rolls past so quietly nobody hears it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ran' reads as the car moving; it is dye running in the wash.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what cannot be heard makes no noticeable sound.

entries.clue: Is at home with good girl — that should clarify things (9)

annotation.surface: Someone stays in with a well-behaved girl, and that ought to settle the matter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clarify things' sounds like explaining a situation; brewers and winemakers literally clarify their drink with this.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: this fish-bladder gelatin clears cloudiness from beer and wine.

entries.clue: American chap called Earl buries old herbicide (5,6)

indicatorNotes.buries: to bury is to put deep inside, so O is buried within the other letters

annotation.surface: An American named Earl hides an old weedkiller in the ground.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Called Earl' looks like a name tag; 'called' is a verb here, and 'Earl' gives only its abbreviation.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: this was the defoliant the US military sprayed over Vietnam's jungles.

entries.clue: Diamonds help to transform porcelain (5)

indicatorNotes.to transform: to transform is to change the form, so HELP's letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Diamonds are said to help turn plain clay into fine china.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Help to transform' reads as a single phrase about improving porcelain; 'help' is the fodder and 'to transform' tells you to rearrange it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the word names the glazed earthenware of Delft, a kind of china.

entries.clue: Ruddy bishop arriving imminently (8)

blocks.note: something looming is about to arrive

annotation.surface: A red-faced bishop is about to turn up any minute.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ruddy' looks like red-faced; it is the mild British swear word, a softened 'bloody'.
annotation.definitionFit: Both are mild British substitutes for 'bloody', as in 'the ruddy bus is late'.

entries.clue: Notices Charles concealing scab (6)

indicatorNotes.concealing: to conceal is to hide inside, so the answer is hidden in the words before it

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap: noticES CHARles

annotation.surface: Someone spots Charles trying to hide a scab.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer runs across the word break, so the capital C of Charles is part of it.
annotation.definitionFit: A medical synonym: the word names the dry crust of dead tissue over a burn or wound.

entries.clue: Terrible excursion around island with a decorator’s assistant (5,8)

indicatorNotes.around: 'around' means encircling, so PANTS is wrapped around I

blocks.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, very poor
per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

annotation.surface: A dreadful outing round an island, taken with a painter's helper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' looks like an anagram signal; it is a British slang word for rubbish, which wraps round the island.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: the solvent a decorator uses to lift old paint off woodwork.

entries.clue: Some early years of school transport company extremely tricky (10)

indicatorNotes.extremely: take only the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'tricky'

blocks.note: a prep school is a private primary school
the first and last letters, T and Y

annotation.surface: Getting a ride-share to school is a hassle in a child's first years.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Early years of school' reads as a phrase about infants' classes; the definition stops at 'years'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the years before puberty are some of a person's early years.

entries.clue: Eventually, neon light damaged bolt (2,3,4,3)

indicatorNotes.damaged: something damaged is broken up, so the letters of NEON LIGHT are rearranged

blocks.note: to bolt is to run off

annotation.surface: In the end, a broken neon sign makes someone flee.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bolt' suggests a lightning strike beside the light; it is the verb, to run away.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: 'over the long term' means in the end.

entries.clue: Conservative provided Trump lifts in illegal trade (7)

indicatorNotes.lifts: in a down clue, lifting the letters turns them upwards, reversing them

blocks.note: to trump is British slang for to break wind

annotation.surface: A Tory backs Trump provided he boosts business in a dodgy trade.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface wants the former president; in British slang a trump is a fart, and the capital letter is only there to fool you.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: as a noun the word covers dealing in illegal goods, such as drugs or people.

entries.clue: Ten entertaining mistakes by fool in Frozen? (6-8)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: a host entertains guests inside the house, so TEN holds the rest
indicatorNotes.by: 'by' means beside, so TRICK stands next to ERRORS

blocks.note: to fool someone is to trick them

annotation.surface: Ten bloopers from a clown in the film Frozen.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Frozen' looks like the Disney film; the question mark says it is a playful definition, frozen with fear.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: fear can leave someone frozen to the spot.

entries.clue: Under control, having attacked king (2,5)

blocks.note: the chess position when a king is threatened with capture

annotation.surface: A rebellion is contained once the king has been attacked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Having attacked king' means having a king that is under attack, the chess sense, not someone who attacked a king.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: restrained, and the chess state of a threatened king.

entries.clue: Vegan points out flag (6,5)

indicatorNotes.out: letters that are out are out of place, so VEGAN POINTS is rearranged

annotation.surface: A vegan pulls out a flag to make a point.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flag' reads as a banner; here it is short for flagstone.
annotation.definitionFit: A short form: flag is short for flagstone, a flat slab for walking on.

entries.clue: Time runs backwards? Extraordinary (4)

indicatorNotes.backwards: 'backwards' means in reverse order, so the letters are read from the end

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

annotation.surface: Time running in reverse would be remarkable indeed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Time runs backwards' reads as science fiction; 'runs' is the cricket abbreviation, not the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something seldom met with is out of the ordinary.

entries.clue: Prototype of fish found by a lake (5)

blocks.note: the ide is a freshwater fish

annotation.surface: The first-ever fish is discovered beside a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: IDE is a crossword favourite among fish; it is a European carp.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a perfect model or pattern to copy, as a prototype can be.

entries.clue: Whale that man’s painting, perhaps, coming back in group (9)

indicatorNotes.coming back: something coming back returns the way it went, so ART is written backwards

blocks.note: an orc is a killer whale, an orca
painting is an example of art

annotation.surface: A man's painting of a whale is returned to the collective.
annotation.walkthrough: 'That man’s' is the contraction for 'he is', not a possessive; 'perhaps' flags painting as one example of art.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a body of musicians playing together is one kind of group.

entries.clue: Rally in park finished (7)

blocks.note: a rec, short for recreation ground, is a public park in Britain

annotation.surface: A protest rally in the park has wrapped up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a noun, a political gathering; it is the verb, to pick up again.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a patient or a share price that rallies gets back to strength.

entries.clue: To understand a person’s character is part of a tailor’s job? (3,3,7,2,7)

blocks.note: the idiom for sizing a person up
taken literally: a tailor takes a customer's measurements

annotation.surface: Reading people is, apparently, part of what a tailor does.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the second half as a playful literal reading of the idiom.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: to size up what someone is like; the tailor reading takes it literally.

entries.clue: I go round every few days in celebration, it’s said, after my horse returned (8)

annotation.definition: I go round every few days

indicatorNotes.returned: something returned is sent back, so MY NAG is written in reverse
indicatorNotes.it’s said: what is said is heard, not spelt, so EDE stands for the sound of EID
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following, so the sound piece comes second

blocks.note: Eid, the Muslim festival, is pronounced 'eed'

annotation.surface: A rider marks a festival after their horse comes home.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the answer itself: 'I' is a moon of Jupiter, circling it about once a week.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: Jupiter's largest moon orbits the planet roughly every seven days.

entries.clue: Try retreating to stop notorious superior (8)

indicatorNotes.retreating: something retreating goes backwards, so GO becomes OG
indicatorNotes.to stop: a stopper plugs a gap, so OG goes inside ARRANT

blocks.note: to have a go is to try
arrant = downright, notorious, as in 'an arrant knave'

annotation.surface: An attempt to halt an infamous boss by backing down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superior' reads as a noun, a boss; it is the adjective, lofty and condescending.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a superior manner is haughty and condescending.

entries.clue: Either Chappell brother who captained Australia’s cricket team concerning Pope (9)

blocks.note: Greg Chappell, Australian Test captain in the 1970s and 80s
'either' is answered by 'or', which joins the two names

blocks.clueFragment: Chappell brother who captained Australia’s cricket team
blocks.note: Ian Chappell, his elder brother, also captained Australia

annotation.surface: A cricket quiz question about the Chappell brothers turns to the Pope.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Either' is spelt out literally: one name, the word 'or', the other name. Greg and Ian Chappell were brothers who each captained Australia at cricket.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the adjective means relating to Pope Gregory, as in the calendar or chant.

entries.clue: Unexpectedly, Joe cries and shows great happiness (8)

indicatorNotes.Unexpectedly: what happens unexpectedly breaks the order you'd predict, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Joe bursts into tears, but they turn out to be tears of joy.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pulls against itself: crying reads as sadness, and the definition is joy.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb means to feel or show great joy.

entries.clue: Back in Irkutsk, has cooked a dish made from buckwheat (5)

indicatorNotes.Back in: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter of Irkutsk
indicatorNotes.cooked: cooking changes raw ingredients, so HAS is rearranged

annotation.surface: Back home in a Siberian city, someone has cooked a buckwheat dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back in Irkutsk' looks like a reversed hidden word; it gives only the final letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a Russian porridge of buckwheat groats.

entries.clue: Monitor temple and church, then arrange golf (8)

blocks.note: a wat is a Buddhist temple in Thailand or Cambodia
to do a party is to arrange it
G = golf in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Keep an eye on the temple and church, then set up a round of golf.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arrange golf' tempts you to anagram GOLF; 'arrange' is a verb meaning organise, and golf gives only G.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a body keeping an eye on others, such as a regulator, monitors them.

entries.clue: Fourteen lines, ten with no structure initially rejected (6)

indicatorNotes.initially: 'initially' means at the start, so only the first letter of 'structure'
indicatorNotes.rejected: something rejected is sent back, so the whole string is reversed

annotation.surface: A poem of fourteen lines, ten of them shapeless, is turned down by the editor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Initially' applies only to 'structure'; 'ten' and 'no' go in whole before everything is turned round.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the classic poem form has exactly fourteen lines.

entries.clue: Disorderly scrap identifying mark (6)

blocks.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
a tag marks or labels something

annotation.surface: A messy fight leaves a telltale mark.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' reads as a fight to go with 'disorderly'; it is a scrap of cloth.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: untidy and disorganised, as in a motley army.

entries.clue: Notes about Republican meeting Conservative in bedroom (9)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means surrounding, so the notes go around R
indicatorNotes.meeting: 'meeting' means joining up with, so TORY comes next

blocks.note: do and mi, notes of the sol-fa scale
a Tory is a British Conservative

annotation.surface: A Republican and a Conservative pass notes about each other in a bedroom.
annotation.walkthrough: The sol-fa notes, do re mi, often stand for syllables in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a shared bedroom for several people, as at a boarding school.

entries.clue: Child departs giggling, having head scratched (8)

indicatorNotes.having head scratched: to scratch is to strike out, and the head is the first letter, so L goes

annotation.surface: A child walks off laughing, scratching their head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Scratched' sounds like itching; in a clue it means struck out, as a horse is scratched from a race.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a female child is one kind of child.

entries.clue: Prompt current referee to conceal millions (9)

indicatorNotes.to conceal: to conceal is to hide inside, so M is hidden within the other letters

blocks.note: I is the symbol for electric current
to referee a dispute is to mediate

annotation.surface: A quick-thinking referee is urged to hide millions in cash.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prompt' looks like a verb, to urge; it is the adjective, quick.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a prompt reply comes at once, without delay.

entries.clue: Getting rid of seating area in attack zone (8,6)

blocks.note: the circle is an upper tier of seats in a theatre

annotation.surface: Clearing out the stands in a war zone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Attack zone' reads as military; it is from field hockey, the D-shaped area in front of goal.
annotation.definitionFit: A sporting term: in hockey this is the zone in front of goal from which goals must be scored.

entries.clue: Outspoken sex symbol, with discretion, shared glance (3,7)

indicatorNotes.Outspoken: what is spoken out is heard, so ICON is spelt by its sound

blocks.note: a sex symbol is an icon

annotation.surface: A brash sex symbol exchanges a discreet look with an admirer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Outspoken' reads as brash; it only tells you to say the word aloud and spell it another way.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: two people looking straight at each other share a glance.

entries.clue: Writer turning blonde, somehow, to give courage (8)

indicatorNotes.turning: 'turning' means rotating round, so ME is reversed
indicatorNotes.somehow: 'somehow' means in some unspecified way, so BLONDE's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the writer is the setter, me

annotation.surface: A writer going blonde to feel braver.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Writer turning blonde' reads as a hair dye; 'turning' acts on the writer alone.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the verb means to make someone braver.

entries.clue: Southern African announced where captive animals go? (4)

indicatorNotes.announced: 'announced' means spoken aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than spelt

blocks.note: a loo, British for toilet, at the zoo

annotation.surface: Someone asks where caged animals relieve themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the joke: 'go' means go to the toilet, and a loo is a British toilet.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this Bantu people of KwaZulu-Natal is southern African.

entries.clue: Finish short of line in run (7)

indicatorNotes.short of: 'short of' means lacking, so COMPLETE goes without its L

blocks.note: L = line; this letter is removed

annotation.surface: An athlete falls short of the finishing line in a race.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Finish' and 'line' read as one phrase, the finish line; they are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to run in a race or an election is to take part against others.

entries.clue: Top lay reader works for one ahead of the game (5,7)

indicatorNotes.works: to work something is to knead it into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: The best lay reader in church does good works for someone streets ahead.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as the reader's charitable deeds; it is a verb telling you to work the letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: someone who takes up new technology before others is ahead of the game.

entries.clue: Lying about Polish family with one item of swimwear (7)

indicatorNotes.Lying about: something lying about is turned about, so RUB is laid down the other way

annotation.surface: A Polish family lounges around, one of them in a swimsuit.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' look like the nationality; it is the verb, to rub.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: a full-body swimsuit, so one item of swimwear.

entries.clue: Composer re-edited Anchorman IV (11)

indicatorNotes.re-edited: a re-edited film is cut and spliced again, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A composer re-cut the fourth Anchorman film.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Anchorman IV' reads as a film sequel; the Roman numeral supplies the I and V.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Sergei, the Russian composer and pianist.

entries.clue: Love is expensive (4)

blocks.note: a pet name, as in 'thanks, love'

annotation.surface: Love costs a lot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the pet name, not the feeling.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: a term of affection, and costly.

entries.clue: Old article covering study by lawyers (10)

indicatorNotes.covering: a cover goes over and round, so THE holds the rest inside

blocks.note: to read a subject is to study it
the Bar is the body of barristers

annotation.surface: An old newspaper article covers a study by some lawyers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a piece of writing next to 'study'; it is the grammatical article.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: worn-out clothes are old.

entries.clue: Cost when monarch and his son stripped of third of land (6,5)

indicatorNotes.stripped of: 'stripped of' means deprived of, so PRINCE loses N

blocks.note: a king's son is a prince
the third letter of LAND, removed from PRINCE

annotation.surface: What it costs when a king and his heir lose a third of their territory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Third of land' looks like a fraction; it is the third letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what a seller wants for a thing is its cost to the buyer.

entries.clue: Very alcoholic beer including drug, at last, for violent wind (6,4)

indicatorNotes.including: 'including' means containing, so the beer holds G
indicatorNotes.at last: 'at last' means at the end, so only the final letter of 'drug'

blocks.note: a strong ale is a potent beer

annotation.surface: Strong beer with a drug in it, the cause of terrible wind.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a toilet joke: strong beer causing wind. The answer is weather.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: force 9 on the Beaufort scale is a violent wind.

entries.clue: Labour’s leader infuriating when ignoring first note for approval (9)

indicatorNotes.leader: the leader of a word is its first letter, so Labour gives L
indicatorNotes.ignoring: 'ignoring' means leaving out, so the first N is dropped from INCENSING

blocks.note: n. = note, as in footnotes; the first N is dropped

annotation.surface: The Labour leader is maddening when he snubs the first memo seeking sign-off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' is not a musical note here; N is the abbreviation used in footnotes, and 'first' matters because the infuriating word has two.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: granting a permit is giving official approval.

entries.clue: More drunk? Rubbish (6)

blocks.note: slang lit = drunk, plus the comparative ending

annotation.surface: A drinker asks for another round and is told it's a bad idea.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags an invented comparative, which no dictionary lists.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: a made-up comparative of lit (drunk), and street rubbish.

entries.clue: Fellow left in pursuit of a scavenger (6)

indicatorNotes.in pursuit of: 'in pursuit of' means chasing behind, so L comes after A

blocks.note: a jack is a man or fellow, as in jack-of-all-trades

annotation.surface: A man left chasing after a scavenger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Left' reads as departed; it is the abbreviation, placed after the A.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this wild dog is known for scavenging.

entries.clue: For example, cow illustration is small (5,4)

blocks.note: a cow lows, so it is a lower
a case in point illustrates something

annotation.surface: A drawing of a cow is only a little one.
annotation.walkthrough: The first piece rhymes with 'mower': one who lows, as cows do.
annotation.definitionFit: A printing term: small letters, as opposed to capitals.

entries.clue: Braggarts primarily seen in hats (8)

indicatorNotes.primarily: 'primarily' means first of all, so only the first letter of 'seen'
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means inside, so S goes into BOATERS

annotation.surface: Show-offs are mostly spotted wearing hats.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Braggarts primarily' tempts you to take a B; 'primarily' belongs to 'seen', and Braggarts is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people who brag.

entries.clue: Setter from the east encountered tourist in Cornwall (5)

indicatorNotes.from the east: in an across clue, east is the right-hand end, so ME is read right to left

annotation.surface: A crossword setter from the east bumps into a holidaymaker in Cornwall.
annotation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in the far south-west of England, popular with holidaymakers, and locals have their own word for them.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: Cornish dialect for a visitor, originally meaning ant.

entries.clue: Relatively small row about European in space (7)

indicatorNotes.about: 'about' means surrounding, so TIER goes round the middle letters
indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means inside, so E goes into EN

blocks.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
an en is a printer's space

annotation.surface: A small quarrel about a European in outer space.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Row' reads as a quarrel; it is a line of seats. An en is a printer's space half an em wide.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the comparative of teeny, so smaller than something else.

entries.clue: Hypothetical particle binding most of protective framework in pancreatic hormone (8)

indicatorNotes.binding: 'binding' means tying round, so GLUON encloses CAG
indicatorNotes.most of: 'most of' means all but a bit, so CAGE loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A physics particle trapping a caged structure inside a hormone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Binding' does double duty in the surface: this particle is what binds quarks, and here it binds the cage.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by type: the pancreas makes it to raise blood sugar.

entries.clue: Free punch during meal, after starter cancelled (7)

indicatorNotes.during: 'during' means in the middle of, so HIT goes within the meal
indicatorNotes.after starter cancelled: the starter of a word is its first letter, so LUNCH loses its L

annotation.surface: Someone gets a free drink at dinner once the first course is scrapped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Free punch' reads as a complimentary drink; 'free' is the definition, a verb, and 'punch' is a blow.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: undoing a hitch, as with a horse from a cart, sets it free.

entries.clue: Have Ken, in advance, regularly peek inside until something changes (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: 'regularly' means at even intervals, so every other letter of 'peek'
indicatorNotes.inside: 'inside' means within, so EK goes into FOR NOW

blocks.note: for now = for the time being
the second and fourth letters of pEeK

annotation.surface: Ken is invited over early to sneak a look until plans change.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ken' is not a man: to ken is to know, in Scottish use, so 'have ken in advance' is to know beforehand.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to know something before it happens is to have ken in advance.

entries.clue: Bar extremely short brown skirts (6)

indicatorNotes.short: 'short' means lacking its end, so VERY loses its last letter
indicatorNotes.skirts: to skirt is to go round the edge, so TAN surrounds VER

blocks.note: VERY with its last letter cut

annotation.surface: A bar bans very short brown miniskirts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extremely short' tempts you to take the outer letters of 'short'; 'extremely' is its own synonym and 'short' trims it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an inn or pub, a place with a bar.

entries.clue: Keen photographer sighs, desperate to take a wee (4-4,2,1,11)

indicatorNotes.desperate: 'desperate' means frantic, so the letters are thrown into disarray
indicatorNotes.to take: 'to take' means to include, so A joins the fodder

annotation.surface: An eager photographer sighs, bursting for the toilet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Take a wee' reads as going to the toilet; 'wee' is the Scottish word for small, the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: very small, usually said of a young child.

entries.clue: Readily available patent number withdrawn (2,3)

indicatorNotes.withdrawn: 'withdrawn' means drawn back, so the letters are pulled back into reverse

annotation.surface: A patent number has been withdrawn but is still easy to find.
annotation.walkthrough: Both pieces are the abbreviations stamped on patented goods, 'Pat. No.'.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from draught beer: whatever is on tap can be had at once.

entries.clue: Argue in flipping crapshoot (4)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' means inside, so the answer lies within 'crapshoot'
indicatorNotes.flipping: 'flipping' means turning over, so the hidden letters read backwards

annotation.surface: Gamblers quarrel over a dice game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild swear word; it means turn over. A crapshoot is an American dice game.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to box verbally is to argue.

entries.clue: Caption rewritten for car company (7)

indicatorNotes.rewritten: 'rewritten' means written again differently, so the letters change order

annotation.surface: An advertising caption is reworked for a carmaker.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is an advertising brief, so the carmaker belongs in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the American car brand once owned by General Motors.

entries.clue: Between New Year and summer in Bordeaux, have confidential meeting (4-1-4)

indicatorNotes.Between: 'Between' means in the middle of two things, so EAT sits between TET and ETE

blocks.note: Tet is the Vietnamese New Year festival
to have lunch is to eat it

annotation.surface: Some time between New Year and summer, a secret meeting in Bordeaux.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Have' sits at the end and looks like a verb for holding the meeting; it belongs to the wordplay, as in having a meal.
annotation.definitionFit: A borrowed French phrase: literally 'head to head', a private talk between two.

entries.clue: Subarctic forest periodically thawing close to tundra (5)

indicatorNotes.periodically: 'periodically' means at regular intervals, so every other letter of 'thawing'
indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its end, so tundra's last letter

annotation.surface: A northern forest thaws now and then, next to the tundra.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is real geography: this forest does border the tundra.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the coniferous forest belt just south of the Arctic tundra.

entries.clue: Call to retreat in Balaclava, for example, at someone else’s expense (7-6)

annotation.definition2: Call to retreat in Balaclava, for example

blocks.clueFragment: Call to retreat in Balaclava, for example
blocks.note: an order to turn cavalry back, as at Balaclava
a telephone call billed to the person receiving it

annotation.surface: A cavalry recall order that someone else ends up paying for.
annotation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade happened at Balaclava in the Crimean War; 'call' also hints at the phone call, known in the US as a collect call.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses: an order to turn a cavalry attack back, and a phone call billed to the receiver.

entries.clue: Reportedly is aware of quiet bridge (9)

indicatorNotes.Reportedly: 'Reportedly' means as people say, so the words are taken by their sound

annotation.surface: Word has it that someone knows of a peaceful bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' reads as a river crossing; it is the part of a pair of glasses that sits on the nose.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by part: the bit of spectacles resting across the top of the nose.
